 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice C.V. Bhaskar Reddy

sentences.text: Order:

This Writ Petition is filed by the petitioners under Article 226 of the Constitution of India seeking the following relief, viz., "... ... ...to issue writ order or direction more particularly one in the nature of writ of Mandamus to the respondent No 5 issued Rc No GPP/illegal Construction/2023 Dt 08/02/2023 for road widening from Moddulagudem Cross R and B road within limits including house No 5-80 through Road Centre point 33 feets two sides for removal of the illegal without any land acquisition proceedings neither payment any compensation without due process of law as illegally and liable to set aside and
violation of Articles 300-A of Constitution of India arbitrary unjust discriminatory in violation of principles of natural justice...

... " 
2. Heard Mr.K. Buchi Babu, learned counsel for the petitioners; the learned Government Pleader for Panchayat Raj, for respondent Nos.1 and 3; the learned Government Pleader for Revenue, for the 2nd respondent; the learned Government Pleader for Roads and Buildings, for 4th respondent; and Mr. R. Chandra Shekar Reddy, learned Standing Counsel for the Pasra Nagaram Panchayat, for the 5th respondent.
CVBR ,

. Learned counsel for the petitioners contended that 1st petitioner herein is the absolute owner of the subject property, bearing H.No.5-80, situate at Pasara Village, Govindaraopet Mandal, Mulugu District and petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are tenants thereof; the 1st petitioner was assessed for property tax by the 5th respondent, and 1st petitioner was regularly paying property tax for the subject property; earlier, the 1st petitioner also filed Writ Petition No.3255 of 2023 on 03.02.2023 before this Court for mutation of petitioner's name in the property tax assessment register, maintained by the 5th respondent.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners further submitted that, as things stood thus, the 5th respondent issued the impugned notice in proceedings Rc.No.GPP/illegalconstruction/2023, dated 08.02.2023, directing the 1st petitioner to vacate the house to enable the Gram Panchayat to demolish the structures existing in the 1st petitioner's property for the purpose of road-widening;
the 1st petitioner is the absolute owner and possessor of the subject property and he is paying property tax continuously, and there is also no dispute with regard to the title of the property; but the respondents, without ::3:: CVBR,J wp_4553_2023 initiating proceedings under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Sri Yanala Anantha Reddy vs The State Of Telangana on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12582739/

sentences.text: 1 Resettlement Act, 2013 and with the influence of local political hierarchy, have forcibly taken up road-widening programme without paying compensation or without issuing prior notice, or obtaining consent from the 1st petitioner; and therefore, prayed this Court to pass appropriate orders in the Writ Petition by directing the respondents not to interfere with the property of 1st petitioner, and allow the Writ Petition.

5. On the other hand, learned Standing Counsel for the 6th respondent, contended that the house of the 1st petitioner is abutting the road leading to Moddulagudem crossroads which is causing inconvenience to public at large; frequent accidents are occurring in the said junction on account of congestion of traffic; in those circumstances, a proposal was mooted by the concerned Gram Panchayat for taking up road-widening; and therefore, the property of 1st petitioner is required for the purpose of road-widening in the interest of public.
: CVBR

In reply, learned counsel for the petitioners contended that the 1st petitioner never gave any consent for acquiring his property; and therefore,
contended that the respondents have necessarily to follow the due procedure prescribed under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 before demolishing the structures in the subject property for the purpose of road widening.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
7. In view of rival contentions of both parties, this Court is of the considered view that the present Writ Petition can be disposed of by directing the respondents to follow due procedure in accordance with provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 for acquiring the land of 1st petitioner for the purpose of road-widening.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Till then, the respondents are directed not to take any coercive steps for demolition of the subject property of the petitioners.
8. With these observations, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
No costs.
CVBR ,
As a sequel, miscellaneous applications pending if any in this Writ Petition, shall stand closed.
_ _ C.V. BHASKAR REDDY, J Date : 16.02.2023 Ndr Sri Yanala Anantha Reddy vs The State Of Telangana on 16 February, 2023
